test_title: PYST 71: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 29 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of these processes begins after pollen lands on the stigma of a flower?

options.text: It develops into a seed directly.
A pollen tube grows through the style to reach the ovary.

solution:
The correct answer is __**A pollen tube grows through the style to reach the ovary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The process of plant reproduction begins with **pollination**, which is the transfer of **pollen grains** from the **anther** to the **stigma** of a flower.
 
• Once a compatible **pollen grain** lands on the **stigma**, it absorbs moisture and sugar-rich secretions from the stigmatic surface, leading to its **germination**.
 
• During germination, a **pollen tube** emerges from one of the **germ pores** of the pollen grain and grows downward through the internal tissues of the **style**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• The **pollen tube** acts as a conduit to transport the **male gametes** (sperm cells) toward the **ovule** located inside the **ovary**.
 
• The growth of the tube is **chemotropic**, meaning it is guided by chemical signals secreted by the **synergid cells** within the **embryo sac**.
 
• Leaves do not begin **photosynthesis** specifically because of pollination; photosynthesis is a continuous metabolic process occurring in **chlorophyll**-containing tissues. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Petals usually **wither** or fall off after successful pollination rather than opening wider, as their primary role of attracting **pollinators** is complete. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Pollen does not develop into a **seed** directly; a seed only forms after the complex process of **fertilization** occurs within the ovule. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Siphonogamy:** This refers to the process in **seed plants** where a **pollen tube** is used to transfer **male gametes** to the **egg cell**, removing the requirement for external water for fertilization.
 
• **Double Fertilization:** A unique feature of **Angiosperms** (flowering plants) where one male gamete fuses with the **egg** to form a **diploid zygote**, and the second male gamete fuses with two **polar nuclei** to form the **triploid primary endosperm nucleus (PEN)**.
 
• **Structure of the Pistil:** The female reproductive part, or **carpel**, consists of the **stigma** (receptive tip), the **style** (stalk), and the **ovary** (swollen base containing ovules).
 
• **Post-Fertilization Changes:** After successful fertilization, the **ovule** matures into a **seed**, and the **ovary** wall develops into the **pericarp** or the **fruit**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Pollen-Pistil Interaction:** This is a dynamic **recognition process** where the **pistil** evaluates the **pollen** to ensure it is "compatible" (belonging to the same species and not self-sterile) before allowing the **pollen tube** to grow.
 
• **Role of Nutrients:** Essential elements like **Boron** and **Calcium** are critical for the successful **germination** and steady elongation of the **pollen tube** through the style.
 
• **Generative and Vegetative Cells:** The pollen grain typically consists of a **vegetative cell** (which forms the tube) and a **generative cell** (which divides to form two **sperm cells**).
